column2: What is the core difference between Amazon SQS and Amazon SNS?
column3: SQS stores messages in a queue for consumers to poll and process; SNS pushes each publication to subscribed endpoints.
column4: SQS supports decoupled work queues, while SNS supports publish/subscribe fan-out.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Messaging topic::Decoupling

column2: An order-processing service must absorb traffic spikes and let workers process jobs independently. Which service is the best fit?
column3: Amazon SQS.
column4: A queue buffers work and decouples producers from consumers so each side can scale independently.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Messaging topic::Asynchronous_processing

column2: One alarm must notify email recipients, a Lambda function, and an SQS queue at the same time. Which service fits?
column3: Amazon SNS.
column4: An SNS topic can fan one publication out to multiple subscribed endpoints.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Messaging topic::Fan-out

column2: What does Amazon EC2 provide?
column3: Resizable virtual compute instances in AWS.
column4: EC2 gives customers control of the guest operating system and application stack on virtual machines.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Compute topic::Virtual_machines

column2: A team needs MySQL but wants AWS to manage the underlying database infrastructure and routine platform operations. Which service should it evaluate?
column3: Amazon RDS.
column4: RDS is a managed relational database service; the customer still owns data, access, schemas, and configuration choices.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Databases topic::Managed_services

column2: What does Infrastructure as a Service provide, and what major control remains with the customer?
column3: It provides virtualized infrastructure; the customer retains control of the guest operating system, applications, data, and many configurations.
column4: IaaS removes physical-hardware ownership without removing workload administration.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Service_models topic::IaaS

column2: How are the AWS Management Console, CLI, SDKs, and IaC tools related to AWS service APIs?
column3: They are different interfaces that ultimately invoke AWS service APIs.
column4: “Single unified API” is only a mental model; it is not the name of one AWS product or one literal endpoint.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::APIs topic::Cloud_management

column2: What benefits does Infrastructure as Code provide?
column3: Repeatable, version-controlled, reviewable, and automated infrastructure provisioning.
column4: Machine-readable definitions reduce manual configuration drift and support consistent environments.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::Automation

column2: Why is Terraform better described as an orchestrator than as an application compiler?
column3: It builds a plan and calls provider APIs to reach a desired infrastructure state; it does not produce an application binary.
column4: Terraform reads HCL and coordinates resource changes through provider APIs.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Infrastructure_as_Code topic::Terraform

column2: Complete the relationship: An AWS Region contains multiple isolated ________.
column3: Availability Zones.
column4: Regions are separate geographic areas, and multi-AZ design provides isolation within a Region.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::cloze topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Regions

column2: What is an Availability Zone?
column3: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within an AWS Region.
column4: AZs are designed for fault isolation while maintaining low-latency connectivity to other AZs in the Region.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Availability_Zones

column2: What is the geographic scope of an Amazon VPC?
column3: A VPC belongs to one AWS Region and can span that Region’s Availability Zones.
column4: Subnets divide the VPC at the AZ level.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Networking topic::VPC_scope

column2: Can one subnet span multiple Availability Zones?
column3: No. A subnet resides entirely within one Availability Zone.
column4: An Availability Zone can contain multiple subnets, but a subnet cannot cross AZ boundaries.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Networking topic::Subnets

column2: An EC2 instance is placed in a subnet whose route table has a route to an internet gateway. Is the instance automatically reachable from the internet?
column3: No. It also needs an appropriate public address and security rules that allow the traffic.
column4: A route makes the subnet public, but internet reachability depends on routing, addressing, and filtering together.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Networking topic::Public_subnets

column2: Why might `us-east-1a` refer to different physical zones in two AWS accounts?
column3: Availability Zone letter mappings can differ by account.
column4: Use AZ IDs when different accounts must coordinate on the same physical Availability Zone.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Availability_Zone_IDs

column2: How can an S3 bucket be Regional while its name is globally unique?
column3: The bucket’s data resides in a selected Region, while its name must be unique across the general-purpose bucket namespace.
column4: A global console view and global naming do not mean that bucket data is automatically stored worldwide.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Storage topic::Global_infrastructure

column2: Which THREE factors commonly influence AWS Region selection?
column3: Latency to users, regulatory or data-location requirements, and service availability or price.
column4: Region choice is a business and technical decision; no single Region is best for every workload.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Concepts day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::multiple-response topic::Global_infrastructure topic::Region_selection

column2: Which two practices best protect the AWS account root user?
column3: Enable MFA and reserve the root user for tasks that explicitly require it.
column4: The root user has unrestricted account access and should not be used for routine administration.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Root_user topic::MFA

column2: Does an IAM user require its own external email address or payment method?
column3: No. It is an identity defined inside one AWS account.
column4: Usage performed by the IAM user is billed to the AWS account.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::IAM_users topic::Identities

column2: Distinguish authentication from authorization.
column3: Authentication verifies who the caller is; authorization determines what that identity may do.
column4: Both are required to securely evaluate AWS requests.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Authentication topic::Authorization

column2: What permissions does a newly created IAM identity receive merely by existing?
column3: None. Permissions must be granted through applicable authorization policies and mechanisms.
column4: AWS access is not granted automatically to a new identity.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::IAM_policies topic::Default_permissions

column3: Condition.
column4: Conditions narrow when a statement applies, such as by source, time, tags, or other context keys.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::cloze topic::IAM_policies topic::JSON

column2: A developer needs read access to one S3 bucket for one project. Which approach follows least privilege?
column3: Grant only the required read actions on that bucket, not broad administrator or all-S3 permissions.
column4: Least privilege limits permissions to the task and resource actually required.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Least_privilege topic::IAM_policies

column2: What are the two parts of an IAM access key?
column3: An access key ID and a secret access key.
column4: Both are used to sign programmatic requests; the secret access key is retrievable only when created.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Access_keys topic::Programmatic_access

column2: How can an IAM user rotate an access key without an abrupt application outage?
column3: Create the second key, update and test the application, then deactivate and delete the old key.
column4: An IAM user can have at most two access keys, which supports an overlap during rotation.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Access_keys topic::Rotation

column2: What is the preferred alternative to long-lived access keys for AWS workloads?
column3: IAM roles and temporary security credentials.
column4: Temporary credentials reduce the risk and maintenance burden of static secrets.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Temporary_credentials topic::IAM_roles

column2: Who patches the guest operating system on an Amazon EC2 instance?
column3: The customer.
column4: AWS secures the physical infrastructure and virtualization layer; the customer manages the guest OS and applications.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Shared_responsibility topic::EC2

column2: Which Lambda security responsibilities remain with the customer?
column3: Function code and libraries, data, IAM permissions, and resource configuration.
column4: AWS manages the underlying infrastructure, operating system, and managed runtime platform.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Shared_responsibility topic::Serverless

column3: No. SCPs set the maximum available permissions for principals in member accounts.
column4: IAM or resource policies must still grant access, and an explicit restriction from an applicable SCP limits the result.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Organizations topic::Service_control_policies

column2: A company needs to record resource configurations and evaluate them continuously against rules. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Config.
column4: AWS Config records supported configuration history and evaluates compliance. Remediation is optional and must be configured.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Compliance topic::Configuration_auditing

column3: Residency is where data is physically stored; sovereignty is the legal jurisdiction and authority governing it.
column4: Compliance requirements may impose controls based on both location and jurisdiction.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Compliance topic::Data_governance

column2: Which AWS environment is designed for eligible U.S. government and highly regulated workloads with isolated Regions?
column3: AWS GovCloud (US).
column4: GovCloud has specific eligibility and access requirements; it is not simply a general Region available to any individual.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Compliance topic::Government_workloads

column2: List the defining characteristics of a security group.
column3: It is stateful, applies at the resource network-interface level, and supports allow rules only.
column4: Security groups evaluate all applicable rules and automatically allow response traffic for an allowed flow.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Security_groups

column3: It is stateless, applies at subnet boundaries, supports allow and deny rules, and processes numbered rules in ascending order.
column4: Inbound and outbound traffic are evaluated separately.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Network_ACLs

column3: Use security groups for fine-grained resource access; use NACLs as coarse-grained subnet guardrails or defense in depth.
column4: Security groups are more versatile because they are stateful and can reference other security groups.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Network_security

column3: No. Response traffic is automatically allowed because security groups are stateful.
column4: State tracking permits the return flow regardless of outbound rules.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Network_security topic::Stateful_firewalls

column3: A network ACL.
column4: NACLs support deny rules at subnet boundaries; security groups support allow rules only.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Network_security topic::Explicit_deny

column2: Is an S3 bucket placed inside a customer VPC subnet?
column3: No. S3 is a managed Regional service outside customer subnets.
column4: VPC resources can reach S3 through public service endpoints or supported VPC endpoints.

column3: Amazon S3 and DynamoDB; there is no additional charge for the gateway endpoint.

column3: It creates elastic network interfaces with private IP addresses and uses AWS PrivateLink.
column4: Interface endpoints can use security groups and normally incur endpoint-hour and data-processing charges.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::VPC_endpoints topic::Interface_endpoints

column3: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint.
column4: A gateway endpoint routes S3 traffic through selected route tables with no additional endpoint charge.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::VPC_endpoints topic::Service_selection

column2: A company needs a dedicated, predictable network connection from its data center to AWS. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Direct Connect.
column4: Direct Connect establishes dedicated connectivity for hybrid bandwidth and consistency requirements.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Hybrid_networking

column3: Amazon CloudFront.

column3: It removes selected objects from CloudFront caches before their normal expiration.
column4: Use invalidation when updated content must be fetched from the origin before its TTL expires.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::recall topic::Content_delivery topic::Caching

column3: Two static anycast IPv4 addresses that route supported traffic through the AWS global network.
column4: Global Accelerator improves network-path performance and failover without caching application content.

column3: Choose CloudFront when HTTP/HTTPS content should be cached; choose Global Accelerator for network acceleration and static anycast entry points without caching.

column3: S3 Transfer Acceleration.
column4: It uses AWS edge infrastructure and optimized network paths for long-distance S3 transfers.

column3: Local Zones place selected AWS infrastructure near metro areas; Wavelength places infrastructure within communications-provider networks for carrier-edge workloads.
column4: Both reduce latency, but the target access environment differs.

column3: AWS Outposts.

column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::Hybrid_cloud topic::On-premises

column3: Regional object storage accessed through APIs.
column4: S3 stores objects in buckets; prefixes create a folder-like view but not a traditional mounted file system.

column3: Elastic shared file storage using NFS.
column4: Multiple compute instances can mount the same EFS file system. EFS does not provide SMB.

column2: Match S3, EBS, and EFS to their primary access models.
column3: S3 = object/API; EBS = EC2 block device; EFS = shared NFS file system.
column4: Choose storage by access semantics, sharing, and workload needs.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::comparison topic::Storage topic::Service_selection

column3: A 1 GB home directory per supported Region, retained until 120 days of inactivity in that Region.
column4: Temporary storage outside the home directory is recycled; CloudShell VPC environments do not have the same persistent home storage.

column2: What are the main functions of Amazon CloudWatch?
column3: Collect metrics and logs, visualize dashboards, and create alarms and automated responses.
column4: CloudWatch focuses on operational telemetry and application/resource health.

column3: Use Budgets for thresholds, alerts, and optional actions; use Cost Explorer to analyze and visualize cost and usage trends.

column3: CloudWatch monitors operational telemetry; AWS Budgets tracks cost or usage against financial or consumption thresholds.

column5: CLF-C02 Billing, Pricing, and Support day::2026-08-28 chat::2026-08-28_-_Gemini_reports_1–7_(consolidated) type::scenario topic::EC2_pricing topic::On-Demand

column3: EC2 Spot Instances.

column4: Containers are typically lighter and start faster; VMs provide a separate guest OS boundary.

column2: Is a cluster itself an orchestrator?
column3: No. A cluster is a logical grouping or capacity boundary; ECS or EKS provides orchestration.

column3: To migrate or replicate databases to AWS with minimal downtime.
column4: DMS supports both homogeneous and heterogeneous database moves.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Migration topic::Databases

column2: A company must keep its source database available while continuously replicating changes during migration to AWS. Which service fits?
column3: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS).
column4: DMS can perform an initial load and ongoing change replication to reduce migration downtime.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Migration topic::Databases

column2: Why might a heterogeneous DMS migration need schema conversion?
column3: Different database engines can use different schema objects, data types, and SQL features.
column4: DMS moves data, but engine differences may require a separate schema-conversion step.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Migration topic::Schema_conversion

column2: Can one Amazon VPC span Regions or Availability Zones?
column3: It can span Availability Zones within one Region, but it cannot span Regions.
column4: Subnets provide AZ-level partitions inside the Regional VPC.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::VPC_scope

column2: Can a subnet span multiple Availability Zones?
column3: No. A subnet belongs to exactly one Availability Zone.
column4: An AZ may contain multiple subnets, but a subnet cannot cross AZ boundaries.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::Subnets

column2: What routing property distinguishes a public subnet from a private subnet?
column3: A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway; a private subnet has no direct route to an internet gateway.
column4: Public addressing and security rules are additional requirements for an instance to communicate directly with the internet.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::comparison topic::Networking topic::Subnets

column2: An EC2 instance is in a subnet with a route to an internet gateway but has only a private IPv4 address. Is it directly reachable from the internet over IPv4?
column3: No. It also needs a public IPv4 address or Elastic IP and traffic must be allowed by security controls.
column4: A public-subnet route alone does not give the instance a public address or open firewall rules.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Networking topic::Public_subnets

column2: What does an internet gateway do?
column3: It enables communication between a VPC and the internet when routing, addressing, and security rules permit it.
column4: An internet gateway is a managed, redundant, highly available VPC component.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::Internet_gateway

column2: Private-subnet EC2 instances need outbound IPv4 access for operating-system updates without accepting internet-initiated connections. What should be used?
column3: A NAT gateway, with the private subnet routed to it.
column4: The NAT gateway initiates outbound translation and permits return traffic, but not unsolicited inbound sessions.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Networking topic::NAT_gateway

column2: What is the core difference between an internet gateway and a NAT gateway?
column3: An internet gateway supports direct internet connectivity for publicly addressed resources; a NAT gateway gives private resources outbound connectivity through address translation.
column4: They serve different routing and addressing patterns and are not interchangeable.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::comparison topic::Networking topic::Gateways

column2: What information does a VPC route-table rule contain?
column3: A destination and a target.
column4: The most specific matching destination determines where traffic is sent.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::Route_tables

column2: Do VPC route tables assign IP addresses or act as firewalls?
column3: No. They select network paths; address configuration and traffic filtering are separate functions.
column4: DHCP-related settings help configure hosts, while security groups and NACLs filter traffic.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::Route_tables

column2: What is the purpose of the local route in a VPC route table?
column3: It enables communication among resources within the VPC CIDR blocks.
column4: Every VPC route table contains local routing for intra-VPC communication.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::Local_route

column2: A route table has 10.0.0.0/16 → local and 0.0.0.0/0 → internet gateway. Where does traffic for 10.0.2.15 go?
column3: Through the local route.
column4: Route selection uses the most specific matching destination; /16 is more specific than /0.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Networking topic::Route_selection

column2: What role do DHCP options play in a VPC?
column3: They provide network configuration such as DNS-related settings to instances.
column4: DHCP configuration is separate from the subnet route table, which selects traffic paths.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Networking topic::DHCP

column2: At what level does a security group apply, and is it stateful?
column3: It applies to supported resource network interfaces and is stateful.
column4: Allowed flow responses are automatically permitted, and security groups contain allow rules rather than deny rules.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Security_groups

column2: At what level does a network ACL apply, and is it stateful?
column3: It applies at the subnet boundary and is stateless.
column4: Inbound and outbound rules are evaluated separately, and NACLs support both allow and deny rules.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Network_ACLs

column2: Contrast security groups with network ACLs.
column3: Security groups are stateful allow-only controls on resource ENIs; NACLs are stateless allow/deny controls at subnet boundaries.
column4: They can be used together for layered protection.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::comparison topic::Network_security

column2: A security group allows an inbound HTTPS request. Does the response require a separate outbound rule for that flow?
column3: No. Return traffic is automatically allowed because the security group is stateful.
column4: State tracking recognizes response traffic for an allowed connection.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Network_security topic::Stateful_filtering

column2: A NACL allows an inbound request. What must be considered for the response?
column3: An applicable outbound rule must also allow the response traffic.
column4: NACLs are stateless and evaluate each direction independently.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Network_security topic::Stateless_filtering

column2: Can one security group be associated with resources in different subnets of the same VPC?
column3: Yes. A security group is associated with resource network interfaces, not owned by one subnet.
column4: The same group can protect supported resources across multiple subnets in its VPC.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Network_security topic::Security_groups

column2: Which VPC control can explicitly deny a malicious source CIDR at a subnet boundary?
column3: A network ACL.
column4: Security groups do not contain deny rules; NACLs can allow or deny and apply to the subnet boundary.
column5: CLF-C02 Security and Compliance day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::single-choice topic::Network_security topic::Explicit_deny

column2: What problem does a VPC endpoint solve?
column3: It lets resources privately access supported services without requiring public internet connectivity.
column4: The client does not need an internet gateway, NAT device, VPN, or public IP for that service path.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Private_connectivity topic::VPC_endpoints

column2: How is an interface VPC endpoint implemented?
column3: With endpoint network interfaces that have private IP addresses in selected subnets, powered by AWS PrivateLink.
column4: Security groups can control access to the endpoint interfaces, and endpoint charges normally apply.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Private_connectivity topic::Interface_endpoints

column2: Which services support gateway VPC endpoints?
column3: Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB.
column4: Gateway endpoints add routes to selected route tables and do not use AWS PrivateLink.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::Private_connectivity topic::Gateway_endpoints

column2: How do interface and gateway VPC endpoints differ?
column3: Interface endpoints use PrivateLink ENIs with private IPs; gateway endpoints add route-table entries and support S3 and DynamoDB.
column4: The endpoint types differ in implementation, supported services, security integration, and pricing.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::comparison topic::Private_connectivity topic::VPC_endpoints

column2: Private EC2 instances need same-Region S3 access without NAT and without an endpoint-hour charge. Which endpoint is the usual choice?
column3: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint.
column4: Gateway endpoints add S3 routes and have no additional endpoint charge.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Private_connectivity topic::Amazon_S3

column2: A private subnet must access a supported AWS service through private IP addresses and control access with a security group. Which endpoint type fits?
column3: An interface VPC endpoint.
column4: Interface endpoints create ENIs in selected subnets and can have security groups.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::Private_connectivity topic::Interface_endpoints

column2: Which statement is correct?
column3: A DynamoDB gateway endpoint uses route-table entries and does not use AWS PrivateLink.
column4: Interface endpoints use PrivateLink; S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints use a different route-table implementation.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::single-choice topic::Private_connectivity topic::VPC_endpoints

column2: Which EC2 category balances compute, memory, and networking for diverse workloads?
column3: General purpose instances, with families such as T and M.
column4: Use workload characteristics rather than treating family letters as official acronym expansions.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::recall topic::EC2 topic::Instance_categories

column2: A batch-processing workload is CPU intensive. Which EC2 category should be evaluated?
column3: Compute optimized instances, such as C families.
column4: These instances provide a higher ratio of compute resources for CPU-bound work.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::EC2 topic::Compute_optimized

column2: An in-memory database needs very large RAM capacity. Which EC2 category fits?
column3: Memory optimized instances, such as R or X families.
column4: The workload is constrained primarily by memory rather than CPU or local disk.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::EC2 topic::Memory_optimized

column2: A machine-learning training workload needs GPUs. Which EC2 category fits?
column3: Accelerated computing instances, such as P or G families.
column4: Hardware accelerators handle specialized operations more efficiently than general-purpose CPUs.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::EC2 topic::Accelerated_computing

column2: A workload needs very high local NVMe IOPS. Which EC2 category should be evaluated?
column3: Storage optimized instances, such as I families.
column4: These instances are designed for workloads whose performance depends on local storage throughput or IOPS.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::EC2 topic::Storage_optimized

column2: Contrast Shared tenancy, Dedicated Instances, and Dedicated Hosts.
column3: Shared is multi-account hardware by default; Dedicated Instances use single-account hardware without host control; Dedicated Hosts give one customer an entire physical server with host visibility and placement control.
column4: Tenancy describes how physical infrastructure is allocated.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::comparison topic::EC2 topic::Tenancy

column2: A license is bound to physical sockets and cores and requires host-level auditing. Which EC2 tenancy option is the best fit?
column3: A Dedicated Host.
column4: Dedicated Hosts expose host identity, sockets, and cores and support targeted placement for server-bound licensing scenarios.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::scenario topic::EC2 topic::BYOL

column2: How does EC2 tenancy differ from EC2 purchasing models?
column3: Tenancy describes physical hardware sharing or dedication; purchasing models describe price, interruption, or commitment.
column4: Dedicated Host and Dedicated Instance answer an isolation question, while On-Demand, Spot, Reserved Instances, and Savings Plans answer cost-model questions.
column5: CLF-C02 Cloud Technology and Services day::2026-09-01 chat::2026-09-01_-_Databases,_VPC_&_EC2 type::comparison topic::EC2 topic::Pricing topic::Tenancy
